title: resilient-helm-templates-for-private-init-cron-and-graceful-rollback-context
author: Maya Chen
description:
Motivation: During private deployments we've seen intermittent failures during upgrades where init jobs race with helm hooks and transient DNS/network errors cause a failed upgrade that can't be rolled back cleanly. This PR introduces a set of templating helpers, stricter values schema validation, and optional init-cron conversion to make upgrades and rollbacks more resilient in VPC/on-prem installs.

What this PR does (summary):
- Adds values.schema.json entries for new fields under `private.init`, `private.rollback`, and `private.upgradeProbe` to validate operator-provided options at helm lint time.
- Introduces template helpers in _helpers.tpl: `private.fullname`, `private.hookAnnotations`, `private.waitLogic` to centralize hook backoff/retry logic and consistent annotation keys.
- Reworks init job and hook templates to: (a) optionally create a CronJob that runs a verify-and-seed workflow before major upgrades (`private.init.cron.enabled`), (b) attach exponential backoff annotations for builtin rollback hooks, (c) expose a graceful-rollback window (seconds) used by the in-cluster rollback operator.
- Adds NOTES.txt updates to surface required values for air-gapped and VPC setups, and a troubleshooting section for common hook failures.
- Adds helm unit-like tests (helm template assertions) and a new integration stage to the GH workflow that runs a local k8s kind cluster for the init-cron lifecycle.

Checklist:
- [x] values.schema.json updated and tested with `helm lint`
- [x] templating helpers added and documented
- [x] Convertable init Job -> CronJob controlled by `private.init.cron.enabled`
- [x] Graceful rollback windows and backoff annotations exposed
- [x] E2E-like workflow (kind) that validates preupgrade init cron and rollback path

Commits (high level):
- feat(values): add schema entries for private.init/private.rollback/private.upgradeProbe
- feat(templates): add helpers and backoff annotation templating in _helpers.tpl
- feat(init): introduce init-cron template and conversion logic from Job to CronJob
- fix(ci): add kind-based integration job and test assertions for hook ordering
- docs(notes): expand NOTES.txt for private installer and add troubleshooting notes

Files changed (high level):
- charts/private/values.schema.json (+new validations)
- charts/private/templates/_helpers.tpl (new helpers)
- charts/private/templates/init-job.yaml (refactor -> supports Job/CronJob)
- charts/private/templates/rollback-hook.yaml (adds annotations + wait logic)
- charts/private/NOTES.txt (docs and troubleshooting)
- .github/workflows/helm-integration.yml (kind test stage)
- tests/helm/templates/init-cron-test.yaml (unit assertions)
- README-private.md (operational notes for operators)

Illustrative snippet (templating helper added):
{{"{{- define \"private.waitLogic\" -}}"}}
{{"{{- if .Values.private.rollback.backoff.enabled }}"}}
{{"annotations:\n  redwood/rollback-backoff: \"{{ .Values.private.rollback.backoff.base }}:{{ .Values.private.rollback.backoff.max }}\""}}
{{"{{- end -}}"}}
{{"{{- end -}}"}}

Review conversation (high level):
- Diego Alvarez (review): "Thanks — overall looks good. Can we make the default cron cadence conservative (once-per-30m) and ensure the job tolerates transient DNS failures? Also prefer feature flag `private.init.cron.enabled` = false by default for existing installs."
- Maya Chen (author): "Agree on defaults, changed cadence to 30m and added retry logic with a 5-retry courteous exponential backoff. Added `private.init.tolerateTransient` flag which defaults to true and only extends wait windows, not aborts upgrades."
- Priya Kannan (review): "Please add a unit test asserting that when `private.init.cron.enabled=true` the rendered resource kind is CronJob and that the annotations include the backoff header."
- Maya Chen: "Added tests and GH action stage — ci now runs a kind cluster and asserts hook ordering with `kubectl apply` + status checks."
- Liam O'Connor (approver): "Verified against a local kind run and an isolated VPC-like network in our staging infra — approving. Leave notes for on-call to watch for any new failures during release window."

CI status and checks:
- helm-lint: initially failed due to schema type mismatch (fixed)
- unit-template-tests: pass
- integration-kind: flaky on first run (network timeout at 2026-02-12), rerun passed on 2026-02-14 after adding additional wait and network retry logic
- e2e-smoke (staging): pass

Merge notes:
- Merged via squash on 2026-02-16 after approvals from Priya and Liam.
- Rolling deployment guidance added to release notes: perform canary upgrade with `private.init.cron.enabled=false` -> enable on a small subset namespace to validate seed jobs -> flip to cluster-wide if healthy.

Operational impact and rollout plan:
- Default behavior is backward compatible (cron disabled). Operators can enable `private.init.cron.enabled` to run pre-upgrade verification/seed workflows for air-gapped clusters.
- If operators rely on custom hook annotations, the templating helper `private.hookAnnotations` centralizes keys; migration guidance included in README-private.md.

Known limitations & follow-ups:
- The kind-based integration stage is intentionally conservative; a subsequent PR (ENG-9124) will expand coverage to multi-node network partition tests.
- We should audit existing install manifests for custom hook keys — an automated linter could be added in follow-up.

release_notes:
- Added optional init-cron for pre-upgrade verification and seeding (private.init.cron.enabled=false by default).
- New Helm helpers for consistent hook annotations and backoff logic.
- Schema validation for private.init/private.rollback to catch misconfiguration during helm lint.
notes_for_oncall: Monitor hook-related alerts and upgrade failures for 48h after release; dashboards: helm.private.hook.failures and cluster.init-job.latency.
operational_steps: Default is backward compatible; no change required for existing installs.
To enable pre-upgrade cron: set private.init.cron.enabled=true and deploy to a canary namespace first.
If custom hook annotations exist, update them to use private.hookAnnotations helper or follow migration guide in README-private.md.
